chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Bukayr ibn Ayn, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).

Regarding a man who stole but they were not able to catch him, then he stole again but they were not able to catch him, and he stole a third time so he was seized. The proof came, and they testified against him for the first theft and the last theft. He said: 'His hand is cut for the first theft and his leg is not cut for the last theft.' It was said: 'How is that?' He said: 'Because the witnesses testified together in one place for the first and the last theft before he was cut for the first theft. And if the witnesses had testified against him for the first theft, then waited until he was cut, then testified against him for the last theft, his left leg would be cut.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on cutting the hand and leg for multiple thefts if the thief is caught after the last one?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia jurisprudential principle that the hadd penalty for theft is tied to the specific instance of theft proven by testimony at the time of execution, rather than a cumulative count of all past thefts. It highlights the critical procedural distinction between simultaneous testimony, which results in a single hand amputation, and sequential testimony, which allows for the full 'cutting of the hand and foot' (qat' al-yad wa al-rijl) for the second offense. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on strict evidentiary timing in applying corporal punishments.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Ali Bi Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, from Bukeyr Bin Ayn,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who stole but they were not able over (catching him). Then he stole again but they were not able over (catching) him, and he stole again, so he was seized. So the proof came, and they (witnesses) testified against him with the earlier ones and the last theft. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘His hand would be cut due to the first theft and his leg would not be cut due to the second theft’. So it was said, ‘So how come that is so?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Because the witnessed testified together in one place with the first theft and the last one, before he had been cut due to the first theft. And had the witnesses testified against him with the first theft, then waited until he was cut, then testified against him with the last theft, his left leg would be cut’.
